issues.title: [RFC]: Qwen-Image 2.1 performance optimization — low-latency, high-throughput, and memory-efficient serving
issues.body:
## Motivation

Native `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` support is merged in [#8099](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8099). We would like community help to reduce generation latency and memory use, improve serving throughput, and turn the available optimizations into reproducible deployment recipes.

**Help wanted:** contributors with experience in kernels, attention, compilation, batching, quantization, distributed execution, or profiling are welcome. Hardware owners can contribute baseline runs, traces, quality comparisons, or reviews. Please pick a bounded item below and comment with your hardware and proposed scope so we can coordinate work.

This follows the community optimization trackers for [SenseNova-U1.5 (#7598)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/7598), [Ming-Image (#8134)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8134), and [MAGI-2 (#7085)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/7085). The serving goals are:

- **A — Low latency:** minimize single-request end-to-end latency and denoising time.
- **B — High throughput:** maximize successful images/s under concurrency while reporting p50/p95/p99 latency and failures.
- **C — Memory efficiency and hardware coverage:** qualify practical configurations for smaller GPUs and additional platforms, with their latency and quality costs recorded.

## Current baseline

Initial source snapshot: [`main` at `3dc35694`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/commit/3dc35694b3d458fc1461a8fe71832ac12e8c8cea). Contributors should record the exact SHA used for each comparison.

The model supports text-to-image and editing with up to four condition images. Request batching, step execution, TP/CFG parallelism, regional compilation, decode CUDA graphs, prefix KV reuse, online FP8, and VAE tiling already have implementation paths. Ulysses SP has partial validation; HSDP and layerwise offload remain marked unverified. Ring attention and pipeline parallelism are unsupported; TeaCache and Cache-DiT are under review ([#9199](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/9199), [#9062](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/9062)). LoRA is wired but lacks real-adapter end-to-end evidence.

Sources: [feature matrix](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/3dc35694b3d458fc1461a8fe71832ac12e8c8cea/docs/user_guide/diffusion_features.md), [recipe](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/3dc35694b3d458fc1461a8fe71832ac12e8c8cea/recipes/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1.md), and [support PR validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8099).

### Published measurements to reproduce

These are historical recipe measurements, not new benchmarks for this issue or universal performance targets. The support PR recorded vLLM 0.30.0, Torch 2.13.0+cu129, and Transformers 5.14.1. The H200 runs used the teapot prompt, 1024×1024, 50 steps, seed 42, and `true_cfg_scale=1.0`; new runs should use and record an environment compatible with their pinned Omni commit.

| Comparison | Configuration | Reported time/image | Quality / memory |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Compile/graph sweep; one warmup, median of three | Compile + graph | 5.93 s | 38.10 dB PSNR vs eager |
| Same sweep | Compile only | 6.88 s | 38.10 dB vs eager |
| Same sweep | Graph only | 9.52 s | Pixel-identical to eager |
| Same sweep | Eager | 8.28 s | Reference |
| Separate eager FP8 comparison | BF16 | 7.34 s | 36.9 GB peak |
| Same FP8 comparison | DiT FP8, all eligible layers | 6.06 s | 30.4 GB peak; 33.0 dB vs BF16 |

Do not combine the two sweeps into one speedup calculation. Graph-only was slower than eager in the published sweep; trace evidence should guide further capture work. Compilation and FP8 also require output-quality comparisons.

## Work items

Ownership updated on **November 7, 2026** from the linked volunteer replies. Every item now has an owner or a covered draft; per-row status links to first reports and open follow-ups. See the [initial coordination and requested cross-reviews](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6062985809) and the [November 7 status reply](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6703954311).

S/M/L indicate approximate scope, not promised effort or speedup. Existing PRs are in progress; coordinate with their authors before starting overlapping work.

### A — Low latency

| ID | Item | Scope | Status / starting point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A0 | Reproduce a baseline and profile text/image encoding, prefix prefill, denoising decode, VAE decode, and response encoding. Share traces and identify the largest measured cost. | S | Complete: [`luca-888`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6056840027). [Report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6061770135) independently rerun on a second H200 ([cross-review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6130580327)): pixel-identical outputs, latency within 1.2%, identical peak memory. Largest cost: denoising, 96–97% of end-to-end latency; GEMM ≈ half of kernel time, elementwise/copy/cast ≈ a third (~1,830 kernels/step). |
| A1 | Fuse or tune Q/K normalization + RoPE, SwiGLU, modulation, and residual operations; measure full-model impact and numerical behavior across GPU generations. | M | Owner: 0z5a via [#7945](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/7945); [plan](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6066223034) separates fusion and 0/6-layer residency variants for separate attribution. Cross-review and additional GPU generations still open |
| A2 | Tune attention and compile/graph execution for 1024/2048 outputs, longer prompts, and editing prefixes. Measure launch overhead, compile/capture cost, graph memory, and eager fallbacks. | M | Claimed: [`nagisa-kunhah`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6042015748). H20; attention and compile/graph profiling, optimization, and correctness validation. Existing compile/graph path; backend correctness must cover block-causal masking |
| A3 | Reduce prefix-KV dequantization, packing, and allocation overhead for long prompts and multi-image editing. | M | Claimed: [`YuDeng0102`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6051183607). A100 40GB; validation and coordinated follow-ups to #7946, whose implementation remains owned by 0z5a. Coordinate with [#7946](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/7946); preserve cache format and attention semantics |

### B — High throughput

| ID | Item | Scope | Status / starting point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | Benchmark and optimize existing request batching versus step execution at concurrency 1/2/4/8/16 where memory permits. Include staggered arrivals, mixed prefill/decode phases, cancellation, and sustained load. | M | First [report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6226309773) posted (A100-40GB, c=1/2/4/8 closed-loop, staggered, cancellation): request batching ≈ step execution at equal batch size; ≤ ~2.6% engine-throughput gain from batching at c=1; p50 rises 28–35% under staggered arrivals; cancellation is the main mode difference. No scheduler change proposed; sustained load remains open. [Shared B1/B2 workload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6226201142) |
| B2 | Profile editing batches with different prompt lengths and reference-image counts/sizes. Reduce padding, packing, and sub-batch overhead while preserving request order and conditioning isolation. | M | First [report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6233473228) posted (PRO6000, 14 workloads): mixed-length batches show larger output drift (27.66 dB worst case) than homogeneous batching; packing overhead measured small. Bounded change proposed: prompt (plus negative-prompt under true CFG) length in `batch_compatibility_key`, graph-enabled serving only; PR to follow against the shared B1/B2 workload |
| B3 | Compare TP/CFG/SP profiles with independent server replicas on the same total GPU budget. Qualify the best latency and throughput configurations separately. | M | Claimed: [`0z5a`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6067807970) on 8×H100. TP=2/4 H200 results exist and stay a separate cohort; true CFG, SP padding, and combinations need dedicated validation |

### C — Memory efficiency, hardware, and regression coverage

| ID | Item | Scope | Status / starting point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Validate DiT FP8, text-encoder FP8, their combination, selective BF16 layers, and FP8 prefix storage across several prompts and editing inputs. Measure quality, latency, and peak memory. | S–M | First [comparison](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6130838641) posted (H200, 7 configurations: DiT/selective-BF16/text-encoder/prefix V and K+V FP8, multiple prompts and edit inputs), [revised per cross-review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6152303526) with a per-case LPIPS ≤ 0.15 gate and dB comparisons. DiT FP8: −16.8% T2I / −15.6% edit latency vs BF16, no recorded failures/OOMs. FP8 prefix storage follow-up stays coordinated with A3 |
| C2 | Qualify model-level/layerwise offload, selective residency, and VAE tiling at 1024/2048 on constrained VRAM. Report transfer cost and actual device peaks. | M | First [report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6142595428) posted (H100/5090/4090): offload+tiling runs all four cells at ≤ 22.69 GiB reserved on 24/32 GB; untiled VAE decode remains the offloaded limit. [#8680](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8680) merged: peak allocated 36.86 → 33.96 GiB at 1024², [edit row confirmed on H200](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6163716714). Recipe convention: peak reserved, per-hardware-cohort tables. Open: untiled 2048² decode under offload on 24/32 GB; residency variants with #7945 |
| C3 | Reproduce and diagnose consumer-GPU TP corruption, then qualify TP/SP/CFG and supported attention backends on additional hardware. | M | Claimed: [`fangfangssj`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6108085424) on RTX 4090 / RTX 5090 / Ascend 910C: BF16 T2I baseline, attention backends, TP/SP/CFG qualification, and a #8135 repro attempt. [#8135](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8135): mixed RTX 5070/5070 Ti + WSL2 report; H200 did not reproduce it. Intel XPU enablement: [#8509](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8509). NPU AdaLN work: [#8005](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8005) |
| C4 | Provision the checkpoint for GPU CI, enable serving/quality tests that actually execute, and add repeatable performance baselines and qualified recipes. | S–M | Nightly 2.1 accuracy ([#8726](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8726)) and perf ([#8923](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8923)) jobs landed. Remaining: the online e2e smoke test still skips without `QWEN_IMAGE_21_TEST_MODEL` and no CI job runs it — claimed: [`latioswang`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6658531002) (A100 80GB; ready-tier placement and checkpoint caching answered in the [November 7 status reply](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6703954311)) |

Cache approximation or fewer-step sampling proposals are welcome as separate experiments with explicit quality gates. TeaCache/Cache-DiT integration must account for the prefix prefill/decode split and calibrate against this model; copying older Qwen-Image coefficients does not establish compatibility. A lower step count or different CFG setting is a changed workload, not an isolated runtime speedup. In progress under these terms: [TeaCache #9199](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/9199) (Qing7364) and [Cache-DiT #9062](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/9062) (nagisa-kunhah), with mutual cross-review requested.

## Evidence and acceptance criteria

Use the shared [diffusion serving benchmark](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/3dc35694b3d458fc1461a8fe71832ac12e8c8cea/benchmarks/diffusion/diffusion_benchmark_serving.py) and [pipeline profiling guide](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/3dc35694b3d458fc1461a8fe71832ac12e8c8cea/docs/contributing/profiling.md) where applicable. Start with one bounded workload; expansion should follow measured bottlenecks.

- [ ] Record the hypothesis, isolated variable, fixed controls, success criterion, run budget, and stop condition before comparison. Pin repository/model revisions, local modifications, environment, hardware/device IDs, backend, inputs, precision, resolution, steps, CFG, and cache settings.
- [ ] Probe feasibility first. Default to one feasibility run and two additional measured runs per configuration; declare a different budget in advance when needed. Exclude preparation and warmups, report variation, and retain commands, raw results, profiler traces, and output images. Do not drop shared caches.
- [ ] Separate startup/download/compilation from process-to-readiness and steady serving. Keep readiness behavior fixed, validate the first inference after readiness, and reuse the prepared environment/server unless startup is the measured variable.
- [ ] Report client latency, engine/stage time, successful throughput, errors, and host/device memory as appropriate. Keep all failed/OOM cases visible; do not pool different hardware or workloads.
- [ ] For kernel, packing, scheduling, and parallelism changes, demonstrate numerical equivalence within a declared tolerance and correct conditioning/order. For FP8, approximate caching/attention, or sampling changes, declare quality tolerances before evaluation; compare against BF16/no-approximation with PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS and visual checks for typography, identity, edits, and RGBA transparency.
- [ ] Validate affected feature combinations and existing consumers of shared changes. Update recipes and feature cells only for configurations with evidence; establish performance regression thresholds after measuring variability.

## Claim a task

Comment with:

```text
Item ID:
Contribution: baseline / profiling / implementation / quality evaluation / review
Hardware: device model, memory, device count, interconnect
Proposed workload and scope:
Success criterion:
Existing issue / PR:
```

A single reproducible baseline, useful trace, correctness test, or negative result is a valuable contribution. Every main item now has an owner or a covered draft, so new volunteers should start from the open follow-ups listed per row (sustained-load serving in B1, FP8 prefix storage in C1/A3, fused-kernel attribution in A1, untiled 2048² decode under offload in C2). We can split claimed work into focused follow-up issues and keep ownership/results linked here.

Feedback is welcome for at least one week from filing; task claims remain open as work progresses.
